articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose and Proton Single Event Effects in AMD Ryzen Processor Fabricated in a 12-nm Bulk FinFET Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The Aerospace Corporation performed total ionizing dose (TID) and proton testing on the AMD Ryzen 3200G processor. The Ryzen processor is a system on chip that contains a 4-core central processing unit (CPU) and an integrated graphical processing unit (GPU). No changes in CPU performance were observed until 600 krad(Si) of dose, while changes to GPU performance were first noticed at 500 krad(Si). Degradation in CPU performance was only observed in processes requiring access to off chip memory, suggesting that radiation effects are most prevalent in the I/O circuitry and not in the digital logic or internal registers.

articleTitle: Proton and Heavy Ion SEE Data on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We present the SEU sensitivity and SEL results from proton and heavy ion testing performed on NVIDIA Xavier NX and AMD Ryzen V1605B GPU devices in both static and dynamic operation.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects and Total Ionizing Dose Radiation Testing of NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX System on Module
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Commercial satellite constellations in low earth orbit (LEO) have benefited from improved radiation performance of advanced electronics as semiconductor technologies have scaled to smaller nodes, allowing them to tap into high-performance processing on orbit with sufficient reliability for their missions. However, for United States Space Force (USSF) missions, further investigation is required to identify the suitability of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) based electronics to meet more challenging radiation environments and mission reliability lifetime requirements. Radiation performance must be evaluated at the module level because some vendors only provide single-board computing (SBC) solutions. It is expected that while the integrated circuit (IC) at the heart of SBCs will have an intrinsic level of radiation tolerance, it is likely that peripheral components, such as regulators and memory, will be radiation sensitive. For this study, proton Single Event Effects (SEE) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) radiation testing was completed on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX using a ProNova Solutions proton beam and AFRL/RV Cobalt-60 panoramic irradiator. Initial results suggest the Orin AGX system-on-module (SOM) operation is limited to 19 krad(Si). This has implications for the feasibility of operating the SOM for short-duration LEO missions

articleTitle: Heavy-Ion and Proton Evaluation of AMD 7nm Versal™ Multicore Scalar Processing System (PS)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper presents the single event response of AMD/XILINX 7nm Versal ACAP dual R5 and dual A72 ARM core processor system (PS) for space applications. The PS was evaluated using Xilinx's System Validation Tool (SVT) design suite. An accelerated particle beam experiment of an XCVC1902 device was performed using the heavy-ion source at Berkeley BASE and proton sources at Crocker Nuclear Laboratory (CNL) and TRIUMF. More than 10 million designs exercising all the PS power domains were generated during the test. The PS single-event results are presented and categorized in terms of detectability and correctability. No SEL was observed in the PS up to a LET of 80 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg, 110°C, and VCCmax operating values. With all PS safety mechanisms enabled, beam test results show that the overall PS SEFI rate in GEO is 0.16 SEFI per year and 1 SEFI per year (at 500km and 51.6° inclination) in LEO. Also, no uncorrectable events were observed in the PS caches and RAMs.

articleTitle: Total Dose and Single-Event Effects Testing of the Intersil ISL73041SEH 12V Half Bridge GaN FET Driver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We report the single event effects and total ionizing dose test results for the ISL73041SEH radiation hardened PWM input 12V Half Bridge GaN FET driver.

articleTitle: SEE and TID Test Results of Radiation Hardened Superjunction P-Channel MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: A family of radiation hardened P-channel power MOSFETs was developed that were the first P-channel FETs based on Superjunction technology. This work discusses SEE and TID test results of -60V, -100V and -200V P-channel MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Total Dose Performance at Low Dose Rate of Isolated Switching Regulator Evaluation Kits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Results of Cobalt-60 low dose rate irradiation of isolated switching regulator evaluation kits are provided. Their performance in the space radiation environment is discussed.

articleTitle: The Aerospace Corporation's Compendium of Recent Radiation Testing Results
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Radiation testing was performed on several commercial components to determine the response of these components to the space radiation environment. Testing was mostly focused on SEE from protons.

articleTitle: Proton Radiation Effect on Barrier Infrared Detector Focal Plane Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This work reports effect of proton radiation on barrier infrared detector with cutoff wavelength of 10.5 and 12.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The results indicate that proton radiation causes slow increase in dark current of the barrier infrared detector. The radiation effect on quantum efficiency of detector is not conclusive. However, the increase in dark current and decrease in quantum efficiency is slow and within acceptable level for an Earth orbit space mission.

articleTitle: SEU and SEFI Characterization of a Frontgrade QCOTS 512Gb NAND Flash Nonvolatile Memory for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Single Event Upset (SEU) and Single Event Functional Interrupt (SEFI) radiation characterization was performed on a Frontgrade quantified-off-the-shelf (QCOTS) 512Gb 3D NAND flash memory. The device was shown to be suitable for space applications.

articleTitle: SEE Test Results for SRAM and Register Files Compiled on 22nm Fully-Depleted-Silicon-on-Insulator (22FDX)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The results of single event effect (SEE) experiments on fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) static random- access memory (SRAM). Testing was conducted using several different ion species from the 88-inch cyclotron at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL). The SRAM and register file structures showed sensitivity to the lowest tested LET (~3 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg), and an approximate saturated cross section around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\mathrm{x}10^{-10}$</tex> cm2, More importantly, the SRAM performance was consistent with earlier tests and extended results by adding register file blocks which utilized full assist structures.

articleTitle: Effects of Neutron Radiation on the Current Transfer Ratio of GaAsP and AlGaAs Optocouplers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This work presents the degradation of the GaAsP and AlGaAs optocouplers as a result of the displacement damage produced by neutron radiation. The devices were irradiated using a (14.5 ± 0.4) MeV monoenergetic neutron beam on the Frascati Neutron Generator (FNG). In particular, the degradation of the Current Transfer Ratio (CTR) parameter is studied, and it can be represented as an exponential function of the fluence for the HCPL-5530, HSPL-5730, IBS-249, IHS-300, OLF-400, and OLS-300 optocouplers.

articleTitle: NVIDIA Jetson TX2i TID and Proton SEE Testing: Results and a Comparison of Two Proton Beam Facilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The NVIDIA Jetson TX2i system-on-module has been radiation tested by The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory. APL tested the devices both for Total Ionizing Dose and proton sensitivity. APL's TID test indicated continuously powered parts fail between 15–25 krad(Si)., though devices failed on reboot if power was removed after 9.7 krad(Si). An unpowered-during-irradiation part failed between 45 and 50 krad(Si), but later had function restored. APL's proton test indicated sensitivity, with both nondestructive and destructive Single Event Effects observed: multiple reboots were required to clear errors, and all four tested boards ultimately failed to boot after a cumulative fluence between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.95\mathrm{x}10^{9}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.37 \ \mathrm{x} \ 10^{9}$</tex> protons/cm-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Error and failure attributions are presented based on post-processed log data acquired during the proton test, implicating the flash memory as a probable cause of the destructive failure. Test parameters and results are compared with those of the recent University of Georgia proton test, further supporting the failure attribution to the flash chip.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset Results from the Radiation Hardened Electronic Memory Experiment in a Geostationary Orbit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Results are presented from the third version of the Radiation Hardened Electronic Memory Experiment (RHEME-3) performed on the STPSat-6 mission in a geostationary orbit.

articleTitle: Irradiation Effects on Power and Timing Characteristics of Commercial 3-D NAND Flash Memories
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of ionizing radiation on the performance of 3-D NAND chips. We observe increased peak current consumption during erase and program operations from the irradiated chip. Additionally, our measurement shows a significant rise in erase time after TID ~ 50 krad(Si), which gradually stabilized after a few months of room-temperature annealing. Conversely, no considerable change was noted in program time. The findings suggest ionizing radiation notably influences the threshold voltages of all MOSFET devices, affecting the operation of peripheral circuit components such as charge-pumps. This may lead to greater chip latency due to slower operations, such as erase operations. The increased peak current draw for various operations necessitates focusing on power, particularly critical for parts deployed in irradiation-prone environments like space, which depend on battery power.

articleTitle: Single-Event Effects Response of 96- and 176-Layer 3D NAND Flash Memories
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Single-event effects testing (heavy-ion and proton) is presented for 96- and 176-layer commercially-available 3D NAND flash memory, with emphasis on SEFI detection and recovery.

articleTitle: A53 SEE Performance in Raspberry Pi and MX8M
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We report SEE performance of A53 processors in Raspberry Pi 3B+ (BCM2837) and MYiRTech MYC-C8MMQ6 (IMX8M). Error correction features and process SEE performance result in significant reduction in SEFI sensitivity.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Zynq-7000 Integrated XADC under Proton Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper presents the investigation of the Xilinx Zynq-7000 system on-chip (SoC) integrated analog to digital converter (XADC) for single event effects (SEE) under proton irradiation. The SoC is equipped on a software-defined radio (SDR) that uses the XADC as system-internal current monitoring circuit to initially detect high current events and to prevent destructive damages of the system. The test results showed minor susceptibility to SEEs under proton irradiation up to an energy of 184 MeV. Nevertheless, the configuration of the XADC is crucial to determine SEEs as discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Consistent and Repeatable Transistor Level TID Transistor Array Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We present 22 nm FDSOI transistor total ionizing dose (TID) induced threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}})$</tex> shifts measured on a packaged array test structure. Results demonstrate high current fidelity and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{t}}$</tex> vs. dose consistency and repeatability.

articleTitle: Comparison of Figure of Merit Calculations to On-Orbit Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper compares upset rates calculated using figure of merit methods to on-orbit upset data. The model is evaluated using data in the published literature.

articleTitle: Qualification of a new Total Ionizing Dose Facility Using a Hopewell GR420 Irradiator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We report on the qualification of a new Total Ionizing Dose facility using a Hopewell GR420 gamma irradiator with a Cobalt-60 source. Device data is correlated to the widely used Gammacell GC-220E

articleTitle: Recent Developments to the Texas A&M University Cyclotron Institute Radiation Effects Facility from 2019-2023
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The Texas A&M University Cyclotron Institute Radiation Effects Facility has made several facility developments in the preceding years including the addition of 9.4 and 15 MeV/u heavy ion beams to the K150 SEELine, a new heavy ion beam to the K500 SEELine, a second ECR ion source for the K500 SEELine, and a remote DUT heating system to both SEELines. The additions of heavy ion beam testing to the K150 SEELine and the second ECR ion source to the K500 in particular have improved reliability and uptime of beam hours provided by the Cyclotron Institute to address the growing demand for beam time in the radiation effects testing industry.

articleTitle: Comparison of MSU and TAMU Heavy Ion Test Results and Evaluation Output Dependencies of SEUs for the LMK04832-SP
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The LMK04832-SP (5962R1723701VXC) produced by Texas Instruments is a space grade JESD204B compliant clock conditioner with integrated VCOs that can provide clock signals up to 3.2 GHz on up to 14 outputs. It went through heavy ion testing monitoring for Single-Event Upsets of the clock outputs at Michigan State University's Facility for Rare Isotope Beams. During the testing, two outputs were monitored to determine if a single ion strike could impact more than one output. The results are compared to earlier test results from testing performed at Texas A&M”s Radiation Effects to determine how well the two facilities correlate.

articleTitle: Total Dose and SEE Testing of the ISL73847SEH Single/Dual Phase Current Mode PWM Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We report the results of total ionizing dose (TID) testing and single-event effects (SEE) testing carried out by Renesas Electronics America ('Renesas') on the ISL 73847SEH current mode pulse width modulator (PWM) controller. The part is a synchronous buck controller that can operate in either single or dual phase mode. It is intended to work with the ISL 73041SEH half bridge gallium nitride (GaN) FET driver and two GaN power stages for point of load (POL) converters used in space applications. The tests were carried out as a part of baseline total dose and SEE hardness verification performed during part development. The part is implemented in a 0.25 micrometer bulk BiCMOS process.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Characterization of the GR716A Rad-Hard LEON3FT Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: GR716A is a mixed-signal radiation-hardened Microcontroller built around a LEON3FT fault-tolerant processor developed by Frontgrade Gaisler. The development of the GR716A was initiated and funded by the European Space Agency within the Embedded Microcontroller for Space Applications activity. The GR716A is implemented using Imec's DARE180 radiation-hardened cell library in a 180 nm CMOS technology platform from UMC. This work presents the SEE characterization of the GR716A Microcontroller based on data collected from irradiation test campaigns performed by Frontgrade Gaisler. The results show an overall SEE error rate below 7.0x10-6 events/device/day for typical space orbits and a SEL immunity up to an LET of 125 MeV.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg,

articleTitle: Single-Event Effects Measurements on COTS Electronic Devices for Use on NASA Mars Missions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper reports recent single-event effects measurements results for a variety of microelectronic devices that include a voltage level translator, bus driver/buffer, DC-DC buck converter, load switch, power protection mux, transceiver, wireless transceiver, and wireless MCU. The data were collected to evaluate these devices for possible use in NASA Mars missions.

articleTitle: High-Energy Atmospheric Neutrons Characterization of Microchip LX4580
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The high-energy atmospheric neutrons single event effects characterization results of Microchip Technology's 24-channel data acquisition system with synchronized motor control interface IC, the LX4580, are presented. The test was performed at the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center. No latch-up occurred during the entire testing and all blocks exhibited great behavior. The use of simple filtering on the acquisition data results in an overall event rate estimated to be 5.8x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup> events per chip per flight-hour at peak flux, well below the target of 10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Xilinx SEM Core on a Zynq-Based Software-Defined Radio Under Proton Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper presents the latest single event effects (SEE) test results of the Xilinx soft error mitigation (SEM) core under proton irradiation. The Xilinx SEM code is used on a software-defined radio which uses the Xilinx Zynq-7020 system on-chip. The SEM core is being tested under different conditions to validate its performance under proton irradiation. In this test, the SEE susceptibility and dependency of programmable logic (PL) utilization and different flux configurations are evaluated. The test results show good performance of the SEM core under low proton flux conditions with no impact of field programmable gate array (FPGA) resource allocation.

articleTitle: Characterization of Low Dose Rate Ionizing Radiation Effect on the Micropac 66266-303 Optocoupler
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper reports Low Dose Rate (LDR) radiation test results for the Micropac 66266–303 optocoupler and presents LDR effects on the device Current Transfer Ratio (CTR). CTR degradations are also compared between 66266 and 66224 (JANSR4N49) optocouplers.

articleTitle: Neutron Induced Single Event Testing of Commercial Ferroelectric Memory Device (FRAM)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Results of neutron induced single event upset testing of the Infineon (Cypress) FM25CL64B-GA 64Kbit (8Kx8) Serial FRAM are described for 14-MeV and moderated 14-MeV environments. Five samples were irradiated with a 14-MeV neutron source. The units were tested after being irradiated statically as well as under bias using multiple combinations of continual read and write/read loops and using a variety of bit patterns. Results for single event functional interrupt (SEFI) and single event upset (SEU) errors are presented along with cross section data and soft error rates.

articleTitle: A Rad-Hard Time-to-Digital Converter ASIC with a Sub-10ps Single-Shot Precision
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: A rad-hard-by-design time-to-digital converter ASIC with a single-shot precision of sub-10ps is designed and validated in a standard CMOS technology. The presented electrical characterization and radiation results demonstrate the in-spec performance of the ASIC.

articleTitle: Combined Displacement Damage and LDR Results of the Intersil ISL73141SEH 3.3V Analog to Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We report the combined results of the high-precision, 14-bit, 1 MSPS SAR analog-to-digital converter after exposure to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \mathrm{x}10^{11},2\mathrm{x}10^{12}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \mathrm{x}10^{13}$</tex> neutrons/em<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>followed by 100 krad(Si) LDR total ionizing dose.

articleTitle: Guide to the 2022 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop Record
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The 2022 Workshop Record has been reviewed and a table prepared to facilitate the search for radiation response data by part number, type or effect.

articleTitle: Review of TID Effects Reported in ProASIC3 and ProASIC3L FPGAs for 3D PLUS Camera Heads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: This paper compares original TID data from ProA-SIC3L FPGAs with existing literature, discusses the impact of different test flows on the TID response, and correlates the data with TID tests of 3D PLUS camera heads.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Testing of the Agilex Commercial off-the-shelf CMOS Field Programmable Gate Array with Protons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Observations of proton induced single event effects on the 10 nm Agilex commercial off-the-shelf CMOS FPGA were made at three proton energy levels. The SRAM-based FPGA was sensitive to protons at these energy levels.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects and TID Characterization of the Frontgrade Technologies UT24C407 Certus™-NX-RT FPGA for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Single Event Effects (SEE) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) radiation characterization was performed on Frontgrade Technologies UT24C407 Certus™-NX-RT Field Programable Gate Array (FPGA). The device was immune to Single Event Latch-up (SEL), exhibited a low Single Event Upset (SEU) cross- section, and self-recovered from most Single Event Failures (SEFs) when the scrubbing option is enabled.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Results for COTS Microcontrollers and Microprocessors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We present single event effects (SEE) results for a variety of microcontrollers and microprocessors. The devices tested include Blackfin embedded processors from Analog Devices, automotive-grade TI and Infineon micro controllers with multiple safety features, and the MSP430FR5994.

articleTitle: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center's Current Radiation Effects Test Results
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: We present results and analysis investigating the effects of radiation on a variety of candidate spacecraft electronics to heavy ion and proton induced single event effects (SEE), proton-induced displacement damage dose (DDD), and total ionizing dose (TID).

articleTitle: Follow-On Testing of the Xilinx Versal Prime
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Results from follow-on neutron testing of the Xilinx Versal Prime adaptive compute acceleration platform (ACAP) are presented. The Xilinx Versal is an adaptive computing platform that is designed to do high-speed artificial intelligence calculations. The Versal VMK180 evaluation board was irradiated in August 2022 at Los Alamos Neutron Science Center (LANSCE). The results are compared to the 2021 results from the same facility. The newer results show more clarity in the single-event upset (SEU) and single-event functional interrupt (SEFI) cross sections.

articleTitle: 2023 Compendium of Radiation-Induced Effects for Candidate Particle Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The sensitivity of a variety of components for particle accelerator electronics has been analyzed against Single Event Effects, Total Ionizing Dose and Displacement Damage. The tested parts include analog, linear, digital, and mixed devices.

articleTitle: An Examination of the Radiation Sensitivity of Electronic Display Pixel Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: 64 MeV proton irradiation test campaigns were conducted on pixel technologies that span the range of commercially available electronic displays for crewed missions. Human-centric optical performance metrics and at-facility characterization techniques are discussed and reported for assessment of pixel radiation susceptibilities.

articleTitle: Accelerated Nuclear Radiation Effects on the Raspberry Pi 3B+ and Pi 4
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: Raspberry Pi™ computers running Linux and embedded benchmarks are subjected to radiation testing in the neutron beam at LANSCE. The ARM® Cortex®-A53 in the Raspberry Pi 3B+ versus ARM® Cortex®-A72 in the Raspberry Pi 4, single-core versus multi-core, and small versus large array SBU cross sections are compared. Results for the A53 and the A 72 are similar. The results of one process on one of four cores and four identical processes on four cores are presented. The results of the array size show that there is more going on than just an increase in size. Linux is helpful in relating some errors that would have been classified as SEFI to an upset in a single bit.

articleTitle: NSREC 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2023 NSREC)
abstract: The Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) is an important forum that allow researchers to publish high quality data about radiation effects on electronics. Most of the workshop deals with actual experimental radiation data collected on commercial or radiation hardened parts. Nevertheless, papers presenting facilities used for radiation effects testing as well as simulation data with the purpose of simulating radiation effects and environments are also welcome. The REDW is held as a poster session as part of the yearly Nuclear and Space Radiation Effects Conference (NSREC) Technical Program. The REDW poster presenters are also invited to write a paper covering their work. The papers are written in the IEEE Transactions format and are included in the separate REDW Record which is published each year after the conference. The papers are also archived and posted in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library. The papers, products tested, test facilities and yearly summaries of the products tested are all searchable using the IEEE Xplore search engine: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/Xplore/home.jsp
